query: What signals suggest a travel expense will be declined?

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Category of the expense item is knowable at submission and plausibly correlates with decline likelihood (e.g., travel vs hardware); external to the outcome.

per_column.name: expense_origin_method
per_column.rationale: How the expense was created (manual/automated/procurement) is a pre-decision attribute that can carry signal about scrutiny and decline risk.

per_column.name: asset_action_type
per_column.rationale: The nature of the action (acquisition, maintenance, travel procurement) is available before adjudication and plausibly relates to approval outcomes.

per_column.name: source_id_present
per_column.rationale: Presence of a source_id (missing metadata) is a legitimate pre-outcome feature; missing provenance could predict declines.

per_column.name: processing_lag_bucket
per_column.rationale: Derived from processed_date; 'not_processed' and processing lag are only known at/after adjudication and correlate structurally with the state itself, leaking the outcome.

per_column.name: submitting_department
per_column.rationale: The originating department is known at submission and can carry predictive signal about approval/decline patterns; external to the focus.

per_column.name: vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor/brand is a pre-decision attribute plausibly linked to policy compliance and decline likelihood.

per_column.name: description_specificity
per_column.rationale: Quality/specificity of the description is knowable at submission and plausibly predicts scrutiny and declines; not a restatement of the outcome.

per_column.name: is_non_standard_item
per_column.rationale: Non-standard items plausibly face higher decline rates; this flag is derivable from the item itself pre-decision, a legitimate predictor.

per_column.name: hardware_asset_subtype
per_column.rationale: Subtype of the item is a pre-decision attribute that can carry signal; external to the outcome variable.

judge.rationale: Nine of ten added columns are legitimate pre-decision attributes (item category/subtype, origin method, department, vendor, description quality, metadata presence, non-standard flag) that plausibly carry signal about whether a travel expense is declined and lie outside the focus variable. Only 'processing_lag_bucket' leaks, since it is derived from processed_date and its 'not_processed' level is confounded with the adjudication state itself. As a set they provide moderate, genuine predictive leverage, though many are correlated proxies for the item type and thus partly redundant with the original 'category'/'short_description' columns.
